newsitem.title: UK: UK business confidence surging - boardroom survey.
newsitem.headline: UK business confidence surging - boardroom survey.

text.p: British business confidence is surging, according to a survey of business chiefs conducted by SBC Warburg.

The survey of over 300 chairmen, chief executives and finance directors of smaller British firms found a positive balance of 45 percent of companies were more optimistic about growth prospects than they were three months ago.
In the March survey, the balance was 28 percent.
But the balance of companies who have raised selling prices in the last year fell from 45 percent to 25 percent, the survey showed.
Service companies are more optimistic than industrial firms with 55 percent of the former expecting higher growth, compared with 46 percent of the latter.

The survey canvassed firms with a market capitalisation of less than 350 million stg. "This survey of smaller companies points to a marked improvement in business sentiment," said Darren Winder, UK economist at SBC Warburg.

"Consumer activity has picked up particularly strongly since the beginning of the year, manufacturing output has started to increase...and survey evidence now points to a strengthening in manufacturing and services activity."
The survey found 45 percent of firms expected at least some unfavourable impact from a minimum wage, which the opposition Labour Party has pledged to introduce if it wins the next general election.
Over 70 percent of respondents said they did not support adoption of the Social Chapter, which guarantees minimum working standards, which Labour says it would sign up for if in government.
